en: Amoghapāśakalparāja 91a 1. ||

Then Vajrapāṇi, the great general of the yakṣas, addressed the Blessed One as follows: "Behold, Blessed One, how the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara has spoken this Amoghapāśahṛdaya, along with the chapter on the maṇḍala, mudrās, and ritual procedures for the present kalpa,
which is exceedingly profound."

It is exceedingly difficult to fathom, exceedingly vast, and exceedingly hard to accomplish; many mandalas, many mudrās, many mantras, and many painted cloths have been proclaimed. O Blessed One, my darkness has departed; they are like the profoundness of the great ocean.
They are comparable to Mount Sumeru;
they are like a mirage, like atoms, and comparable to the wisdom of a Tathāgata.
Beyond calculation, incomparable, immeasurable,
infinite;
they are the number of incalculable eons and the measure of those eons.
They have the measure of inconceivable eons;
they have the measure of the domain of the gods;
they have the measure of the domain of the nāgas; they have the measure of the domain of sentient beings.
The Tathāgatas are immeasurable and inconceivable; they are immeasurable in the manifestation of the Tathāgata’s eye; they are immeasurable in the illumination of the Tathāgata’s wisdom.
The measure of the wisdom of Bodhisattvas;
the measure of the realm of Māra.
Not before, O Blessed One...
Neither a beginning is perceived,
nor a middle is perceived,
nor an end is perceived.
Therefore, O Blessed One, how may I grant permission?
By the ritual procedure of which [deity] shall I accomplish [the rite]?
Which mantra? Which mudrā? In which maṇḍala? Which painted mudrā? Which hand-mudrā? What is the application of incense? What is the collyrium? What is the pill?
What is the incense? What is the cotton cloth? What is the root mantra? What is the heart mantra? What is the near-heart mantra?
What is the wrathful mantra?
What is the fierce one? What is the gentle one?
What is the single syllable? What is the two-syllable [mantra]? What is the three-syllable? What is the four-syllable?
What is the five-syllable? What is the six-syllable? What is the seven-syllable? What is the eight-syllable?
What is the nine-syllable [formula]? What is the ten-syllable [formula]?
How is the fast observed? How...
How is the ritual for bathing performed during the day and night? How is the clothing donned? How is the binding of the directions performed? How is the binding of the mandala performed?
How is the binding of the topknot performed?
How is self-protection performed? How is the protection of others performed? How is the protection of one’s companions performed?
How is the protection of disciples performed?

How is entry [into the mandala] performed? How is prostration performed? How is circumambulation performed? (6) How is the offering of water for the feet and the guest-water performed? How is the offering of the bali-oblation performed? How is the offering of flowers performed?
How [should one offer] incense? How [should one offer] perfumes? How [should one offer] lamps? How [should one perform] the ritual rinsing (upaspṛśana)?
How [should one offer] the food offering (nivedana) in all cases?
How is there summoning? How is there invitation? How is there the exhortation through dreams?
What is the ritual procedure for the fire sacrifice (*homa*)?

Which is the rite of pacification (*śāntika*), which is the rite of enrichment (*pauṣṭika*), and which is the rite of sorcery (*abhicāruka*)? What is the noose (*pāśa*), what is the vajra, what is the lotus (*padma*), and what is the dismissal (*visarjana*)?
“Blessed One, I do not know to whom one should go for refuge; what are the characteristics and signs [of such a person], and what kind of conduct does he have?
Blessed One, toward what ritual procedure for accomplishing activities shall I conform? And how, in the final age, in the final time, shall I act for the sake of sentient beings?”
"To whom shall I grant success?
How shall I deliver sentient beings?
O Blessed One, I am thus perplexed."
“O Blessed One, I am devoid of eloquence; it is not possible for me to know that.
Therefore, O Blessed One, tell me its characteristics according to the prescribed method.”
I have a doubt, O Blessed One; may the Blessed One cut through my doubt.

Then the Blessed One Śākyamuni, the Tathāgata, Arhat, and Samyaksaṃbuddha, having heard the Tathāgata being questioned with a question concerning reality, spoke thus to Vajrapāṇi, the great yakṣa general.

Excellent, excellent, Vajrapāṇi! This question is most difficult to obtain; well asked, Vajrapāṇi, has eloquence arisen for you in this inquiry. You are compassionate, Vajrapāṇi, in asking for the benefit and welfare of all sentient beings. For those who ask for the sake of the supreme accomplishment of all vidyādharas, this is most wonderful, Vajrapāṇi—whether asked or unasked—is this procedure of the Great Kalparāja, the Amoghapāśahṛdaya, which is equal to the illusion-like samādhi, Vajrapāṇi.

This is equal to the depth of the great ocean, being difficult to fathom; it is not possible for Vajrapāṇi to count the drops of the great ocean, nor is it possible to grasp the measure of the Amoghapāśahṛdaya.
And, O Vajrapāṇi, it might be possible by calculation to determine the limit of this Sumeru, king of mountains, if it were scattered into the finest atoms;
yet, once again, the Sumeru, king of mountains, would remain and be established [as before].
And as for my own capacity,

O Vajrapāṇi, it is not possible for me to grasp the full extent of this *Amoghapāśahṛdayakalpa*; it is so vast, so difficult to penetrate, and so profound that it cannot be mastered even by all the Tathāgatas.

It is for the purpose of penetrating the knowledge of the minds of those in the past, future, and present; but it is not for the purpose of grasping the measure of an eon or the heart of the *Amoghapāśa*. O Vajrapāṇi, that which is like an illusion is this *hṛdaya*; that which is meditative absorption (*samādhi*) is the noose. This is the miraculous manifestation of the *māyopama-samādhi* (the illusion-like absorption).
The Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara manifests in various forms, colors, marks, and shapes for the sake of liberating all sentient beings.
O Vajrapāṇi, this Avalokiteśvara, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, is the supreme achiever of success for all vidyādharas; he runs everywhere equally.
Where the milk and water meet, there he flows together with them.
Great loving-kindness and compassion pervade everywhere equally;
with the unfailing lasso,
one draws them forth and delivers them.
He establishes them upon the adamantine mandala at the site of immortality.

Whether low, superior, or middling, of humble or noble lineage, or belonging to the realms of hell, animals, or the world of Yama—everywhere, by the mere act of recollection, naming, or grasping [the name], he hastens to all sentient beings and delivers them. Furthermore, he does not experience fatigue, exhaustion, regret, pride, or aversion.
Among the gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, rākṣasas, bhūtas, apasmāras, pretas,
and in the forests, in the abodes of Yama, and even within the depths of Pātāla— from the peak of existence (bhavāgra) down to the Avīci hell,
and up to the Akaniṣṭha heaven— he courses through them all with a single mental impulse.
It delivers all beings— including gods and nāgas, as well as those of the three realms of existence, women, men, boys, and girls—
just as the rays of the sun dispel all darkness everywhere throughout Jambudvīpa.
They illuminate.
In the same way, the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara illuminates everywhere with great compassion.
Equally (sama), they abide everywhere;
they completely liberate [beings] from all painful sensations, fears, terrible diseases, sorrows, sufferings, and bonds;
they completely liberate them from the sufferings of birth, old age, and death.
He establishes them on the path leading to all the heavens.
In this way, his great compassion and great loving-kindness extend equally everywhere;
he delivers all beings equally everywhere.
He establishes all beings equally upon the path to enlightenment;
he becomes equally a refuge and ultimate resort for all.
Thus, O Vajrapāṇi, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, with such firm armor and zeal, is dedicated to the welfare of all vidyādharas and all sentient beings.
This Great Caravan Leader, O Vajrapāṇi, leads all sentient beings along the path of great fear; he establishes them on the secure and auspicious path,
and he proceeds without conceptualization, without discursive thought, and without any alteration.
And his mind does not become remorseful.

Then indeed, Vajrapāṇi, the great yakṣa general, having heard this praise of the great qualities of the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara in the presence of the Blessed One, was satisfied, elated, joyful, and filled with gladness and mental well-being; he uttered this inspired utterance:
"Oh, the Lord of Lokeśvara!
Oh, the Guru Lokeśvara! By the manifestation of the qualities of your name, all are liberated from miserable rebirths.
Thus spoke the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi.
This Lord is the teacher of the world; this Lord is the grandfather in the world;
this Lord is the deliverer from the world, O Sage, like the sun during the day.
The Blessed One spoke this.
It is even so, Vajrapāṇi, just as you have said.
The Blessed One said:

4. Go, Vajrapāṇi! Pay homage to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara and inquire [of him]. He will show you his true speech according to the ritual procedure, revealing the essential nature of the *hṛdaya*. Just as he will demonstrate the accomplishment and the means for achieving the rite of the *Amoghapāśahṛdayakalpa*.
And he teaches.

Then Vajrapāṇi, the great yakṣa general, who moves with a most profound gait and walks with the stride of a lion, brandishing his vajra and holding a moon-disc and celestial flower, approached the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara.

He approached him; having approached, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Noble Avalokiteśvara bowed his head at [the Buddha's] feet, circumambulated him three times to the right, placed his right knee upon the ground, and with a moon-like stainless flower, addressed the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Noble Avalokiteśvara as follows: 6. Thus he spoke.
"O Blessed One,
I have not fallen into delusion, nor has my mindfulness been lost or my intellect contracted;
this [teaching] is exceedingly vast."
In the *Amoghapāśahṛdaya*, there are many mantras, mudrās, and procedures for the practice of the cloth-painting (*paṭaduṣya*).

I do not know which is the beginning, which is the middle, and which is the conclusion; which is the root-mantra (*mūlamantra*), which is the heart-mantra (*hṛdaya*), which is the near-heart-mantra (*upahṛdaya*), and what is the ten-syllable mantra; and what is the ritual manual (*kalpa*) for the mandala on the cloth? O Blessed One, please grant me the opportunity [to learn this]. Thus [he said].

Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, out of compassion for Vajrapāṇi, took a flower as pure as the radiance of the moon and cast it into the expanse of the sky as an offering to the Blessed One.
As soon as it was cast, it remained above the crown of the Blessed One’s head in the form of a wheel,
five hundred yojanas in width and rising far above the earth.

"Remain as far as the Akaniṣṭha heaven! [It is] a staff of great blue vaidūrya, with bells of Jāmbūnada gold hanging from it; it is a radiant binding of silk, blazing, well-formed, perfectly circular, wheel-shaped, illuminated by more than a hundred thousand times ten million suns, utterly pure, cleansed, stainless, like a golden chain."
Well-established and resplendent.
It was inlaid with various great maṇi-jewels, delightful, fulfilling desires, gladdening, and lovely to behold;
it was worthy of being venerated and worshipped by gods and asuras, praised by ṛṣis, and prophesied by the Blessed Buddhas.

And everywhere, the assembly circles were seated within a gabled pavilion made of the seven precious gems, which was pure like the luster of the moon and adorned with flowers, filaments, and the forms of Tathāgatas seated upon them—[all] beneath the parasol.
A complete circle of divine celestial palaces;
gods, nāgas, apsarases, divine maidens, nāga maidens, kinnara maidens,
and [other] gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, and kinnaras.

Hundreds of thousands of mahoragas and vidyādharas, along with vidyādharīs, bore celestial flower-vimānas adorned with divine ornaments, garments, and finery; they carried decorative bands, banners, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, standards, and flags.

They honored the Blessed One and the circle of the assembly, raining down clouds of various divine offerings and providing for worship with divine gandharva songs, music, and the playing of cymbals and drums.

On Mount Potalaka, within the assembly circle together with their celestial palaces, they raised a great shout of joy; and those gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas who dwell on Mount Potalaka were filled with exultation.
He was struck with wonder at those deities of the Tathāgata-family maṇḍala and those deities of the Padma-family maṇḍala.
And those deities of the Vajra-family maṇḍala; and those deities of the Maṇi-family maṇḍala; and those deities of the Gaja-family maṇḍala.
And all those deities of the great maṇḍala were filled with supreme wonder.
Attaining a sense of wonder and filled with exultation,
they remained gazing up at the Blessed One, struck by amazement.

And those deities of the moon, sun, lunar mansions, and clusters of stars; the night deities; Śakra, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Maheśvara, Kumāra, Nandikeśvara, Gaṇeśvara, Mahākāla, Īśvara, Maheśvara, the divine son Brahmādevaputra, and the four Great Kings;
as well as the deities Māṇibhadra, Pūrṇabhadra, Baladeva, Yama, Varuṇa, Kuvera, and Kumāra—holding parasols and staffs, they honored the Blessed One.

With great celestial palaces and through divine transformations, clouds of offerings rained down from all sides in the shape of parasols; meanwhile, within, the Tuṣita gods and the Akaniṣṭha gods, surrounded by hosts of devaputras in all the celestial abodes, [honored him].

In the sky, with great clouds of offerings, worship of the Blessed One Śākyamuni and Avalokiteśvara within the assembly circle is being performed; and those earth-deities, nāgas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, gandharvas, and earth-deities [nāgas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, gandharvas, and earth-deities]— [...they too perform the worship.]
The deities of the waters;
the deities of the forests;
the deities of the crops.
All those medicinal deities purified their celestial palaces on the surface of the earth.
Sprinkled with various scented waters and anointed with various powdered perfumes.
They adorned the circles of the earth, scattering various flowers and perfuming them with various incenses.
Thus [is] the miraculous manifestation of vast space,
the bull-like majesty of the Tathāgata, and the empowerment of the Tathāgata’s samaya.
Then Vajrapāṇi, the great general of the yakṣas,
having seen such vast and extensive great miraculous transformations, was seized with extreme wonder and attained a state of amazement.
He thought thus:
"This is most wonderful! It has been displayed by the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara."
Then Vajrapāṇi, the great general of the yakṣas, again entreated the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara:
"O Blessed One, please grant me the opportunity."
Then the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara said this to Vajrapāṇi, the great general of the yakṣas:
"Vajrapāṇi, show favor by dispelling doubts and cutting through uncertainty."

Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, the Noble Avalokiteśvara, rose from his seat, joined his palms in reverence toward the Blessed One, circumambulated him three times, and standing before the Blessed One with unblinking eyes and a smiling countenance, his body ablaze with rays of light, addressed the Blessed One as follows:
Blessed One, I possess the Padmodāravikurvaṇa Maṇḍala within the Amoghapāśa Maṇḍala,
and the Padmoṣṇīṣamaṇi Maṇḍala.
In the secret [chapter] of the Amoghapāśa,
in the chapter on the great maṇḍala of Samantāvalokita, concerning the illusion-like heart-seal,
that I...
O Blessed One, I shall proclaim it before the Blessed One.
I shall reveal the heart-mantras that accomplish the means to happiness when recited, which are the true essence of the samaya.

Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, extended his golden-colored arm, adorned with hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of various rays of light, and placed his hand upon the head of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, saying: "Excellent, excellent, O Great Pure Being!"
"Speak, O Avalokiteśvara, whenever you deem it the right time.
Then the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, having understood the Blessed One’s request and having gazed toward the ten directions,
paid homage to all the Tathāgatas.
Having gazed upon all the Tathāgatas, he spoke the root mantra, the Amoghapāśa-padmoṣṇīṣa-maṇi, the heart-mantra of Amoghapāśa: || ||

Homage to all the Tathāgatas who abide throughout the three times, to the Unfailing Uṣṇīṣas, and to the Unfailing Secret Maṇḍalas; homage to all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas! Homage to the assemblies of all Pratyekabuddhas and Noble Śrāvakas of the past, future, and present! Homage to the heart-samayas of the secret family of all Tathāgatas!
Homage to those who have gone rightly; homage to those who have practiced rightly.
Homage to the Greatly Wise Śāradvatīputra.
Homage to the noble assembly of the foremost great Bodhisattvas, headed by the noble Maitreya. Homage!

To the noble Amitābha, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Perfectly Awakened One; homage to the Three Jewels; homage to the noble Avalokiteśvara, the Bodhisattva, the Mahāsattva, the wearer of the Padmoṣṇīṣa and the holder of the maṇḍala.
Having paid homage to those great sages, the most excellent assembly of noble ones who possess great compassion, I shall [explain] this maṇḍala of liberation,
which was uttered from the mouth of the noble Avalokiteśvara.

O Heart of the Amogharāja Padmoṣṇīṣa, spoken in the presence of the Tathāgata before a great assembly, I shall now recite it. May they be successful for the monk Śīlākaragupta in all his undertakings; may there be protection from all fears.
Namely: Oṃ padmoṣṇīṣavarada hūṃ.
Cara cara ciri ciri curu curu Mahākāruṇika! Ciri ciri piri piri ciri ciri Paramakāruṇika!
Siri siri!
ciri ciri | piri 2. piri viri viri mahāpadmahasta(m) | kala kala |
*Kili kili kulu kulu, O Great Pure Being! Come, come! Awaken, awaken! Run, run!
Kaṇa kaṇa kiṇi kiṇi kuṇu kuṇu, O Supreme Pure Being!
Act, act kiri kiri kuru kuru, O One Who Has Attained Great Power!*

Move, move! Move about, move away! Eṭaṭa eṭaṭa! Bhara bhara! Bhiri bhiri! Bhuru bhuru! O you who are free from passion, adorned with the great pure lotus uṣṇīṣa, accomplish it! Hūṃ hūṃ! (8) Come, come, O Great Compassionate One, wearer of the great garb of Paśupati! Dhara dhara, wearer of the great lotus uṣṇīṣa!
Sara sara, you who remove all obscurations! Cara cara, you who are honored by all the vidyādharas!
Hara hara, you who remove all sins!
Hā hā hā hā! Hī hī hī hī!
Hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ! Wearing the guise of Brahmā Oṃkāra!
Dhara dhara dhiri dhiri dhuru dhuru, O holder of the flame of the great lotus! Tara tara sara sara para para, O holder of the lotus-noose! Cara cara!
O you whose body is adorned with hundreds of thousands of excellent, excellent, most excellent rays!

Blaze, blaze! Heat, heat! O Blessed One, whose feet are worshipped by the hosts of sages, gods, and the deities Soma, Āditya, Yama, Varuṇa, Kubera, Brahmā, and Indra! Suru, suru! Curu, curu! Puru, puru! Muru, muru!
O God, who assumes many various guises as Māra, Rudra, Vāsava, Viṣṇu, Dhanada, and the Lord of Ṛṣis!
Holder of the great lotus-staff,
holder of the noose; dhara dhara, dhiri dhiri.
Dhuru dhuru, thara thara, ghara ghara, yara yara, lara lara;
hara hara, para para.
Para para!
O you who move and do not move, O bestower of the supreme great boons!
O Lokeśvara, beholder of the entire maṇḍala, O Great Lord!

Muhu muhu | Muru muru muya muya muñca muñca | O Blessed One, Noble Avalokiteśvara, protect, protect me, Śilākaragupta, from all fears, from all calamities, from all planetary influences, from all fevers, from all diseases, and grant liberation from execution, imprisonment, beating, threats, kings, thieves, robbers, fire, water, poison, and weapons.
Kaṇa kaṇa kiṇi kiṇi! Kuṇu kuṇu!
Move, move, O illuminator of the faculties, the powers, the factors of enlightenment, and the four noble truths!
Tama tama dama dama sama sama | sama sama, O dispeller of the great darkness of deep gloom! Fulfilled one of the six perfections, mili mili!
ṭaṭa ṭaṭa | ṭhaṭha ṭhaṭha ṭiṭi ṭiṭi ṭhiṭhi ṭhiṭhi | ṭuṭu ṭuṭu ṭhuṭhu ṭhuṭhu |
Girt with a belt of eneya-deer skin!
Come, come, O Īśvara, Maheśvara, Padmeśvara, destroyer of the hosts of great bhūtas! O Mahāsiddheśvara, act, act! Pass beyond, pass beyond!
Kaṭa kaṭa! Maṭa maṭa!
O Greatly Compassionate One, dweller in the pure realm, [clad in] a white sacrificial thread! (9)
Wearing a crown and garland of jewels,
with a most wonderful crown placed upon the head of the Omniscient One,
his palms joined in the form of a lotus, he is absorbed in meditation, concentration, and liberation.
O Great Compassionate One who causes the continuums of many sentient beings to tremble [with faith] and brings them to maturity;
who purifies all karmic obscurations; who liberates from all diseases;
who fulfills all hopes.
O consoler of all sentient beings! Oṃ! To the heart-mantra mandala of Padmoṣṇīṣapāśa, homage be to you! Svāhā!
And immediately upon these words being spoken by the Noble Avalokiteśvara— the Amoghapāda,
Padmoṣṇīṣa, Guhya-hṛdaya, and Maṇḍala— this great trichiliocosm world-system experienced a massive earthquake,
including its mountains, forests, and groves.
The earth began to tremble in six ways.

And upon the entire surface of the earth, a lotus-throne made of the seven precious gems appeared everywhere. From the navel of the Blessed One, a great lotus emerged, possessing a thousand petals, made of the seven precious gems, with a stalk of great blue lapis lazuli, a pericarp of Jambū-river gold, filaments of red pearls, and divine, great pearl-pollen.
It became a single mass of flame,
emitting various rays of light,
namely blue, yellow, red, and white.
Illuminated by the colors of emerald, madder, crystal, and silver, it blazes, shines, and radiates brilliantly; it illuminates all Buddha-fields throughout the ten directions.
It illuminates and gladdens all the abodes of the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas.
He exhorts them and comforts them;
having illuminated and touched them with the sixteen great hells, those great hells appear as a vast lotus pond.
And those hell-beings, by the mere touch of that radiance,
were all completely liberated; they were reborn through spontaneous birth (*upapāduka*) within lotuses in the world-system of Sukhāvatī,
possessing divine bodies adorned with ornaments, finery, garments, and accoutrements, and becoming those who remember their births in every successive life.

Thus, having illuminated those who had gone into the animal realm— the beasts and birds— all those who had gone into the animal realm were completely liberated and reborn in the heavens, wearing swaying, stainless earrings. In this way, [he illuminated] all sentient beings throughout the ten directions.
Touched by that radiance,
they all became established upon the eight great stages (*mahābhūmi*).
And by that, the great assemblies of bodhisattvas gathered there were all established in the state of non-retrogression regarding unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.

And all those in the assembly of the Vidyādharas obtained the secret heart-mantra of the Great Amoghapadmoṣṇīṣa and the accomplishment of the Amoghapāśa. And all those in the assembly of the Nāga kings were illuminated by the Cintāmaṇidhvaja.
And all those in the assembly of the gods obtained the Jvalanolkā-samādhi.
And those who were the assemblies of yakṣas, rākṣasas, and sarpas, they all came to dwell in palaces made of jewels;
and those who were the assemblies of bhūtas, they all attained the samādhi of stainless splendor.
And those who were of the assembly of asuras all became armored with the adamantine armor and the adamantine banner.
And those who were of the assembly of garuḍas became possessed of great peaks with adamantine beaks and attained powerful speed.
And those who were of the assembly of kinnaras and mahoragas all became pure in body, speech, and mind.

And all those laymen, laywomen, men, women, boys, and girls became completely liberated from the suffering of birth, old age, and death. From the body of the Blessed One, a great ray of light named Sūryaketu was emitted; it entered the heart of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Āryāvalokiteśvara. As soon as it had entered the heart of Avalokiteśvara, Vajrapāṇi, the great general of the yakṣas, said this to him:
"Behold, Vajrapāṇi, the miraculous manifestation of the secret heart-mantra of Amoghapāśa-Padmōṣṇīṣa!
Vajrapāṇi said:

"I have seen it, O Blessed One; I have seen it, O Pure Being! This great Pure Being, Padmeśvara Amoghapāśa, possesses inconceivable miraculous transformations. Pray, O Blessed One, speak in full detail of this most profound and vast secret heart-maṇḍala, the supreme accomplishment of the most wonderful sādhanas. (11) [The Chapter on Mantras] (Mantrapaṭala)

"Speak, in the presence of the Tathāgata, this wondrous ritual procedure for the maṇḍala of ignorance, for the purpose of destroying the evil of all sentient beings and for the sake of the supreme accomplishment of the holders of the vidyā-mantras.
Then the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara—
He spoke thus to Vajrapāṇi, the great general of the yakṣas:
"Vajrapāṇi, favor this Amoghapāśa-hṛdaya, the supreme secret;
it is the mandala of all uṣṇīṣas for the benefit of all sentient beings, the destroyer of all evil, and the purifier of all obscurations."
It carries away all impurities and turbidity, pacifies all diseases, wards off all misfortunes,
and subdues the fear of all sins, wicked beings, adversaries, and enemies.
It subdues all obstructors and leaders of impediments; it utterly crushes all wicked ones such as Māras and the like;
and [it protects from] the fear of all poisons, weapons, fire, water, venomous serpents, and lions.
It wards off royal consumption and [other] diseases; it destroys all poisons, malevolent spirits (*kākhorda*), and the application of sprinkled powders.
This is the heart-mantra of Amoghapāśa, the marvelous essence of reality.
And the *Sādhanatattvasāra* states: "The supreme accomplishment is attained through recitation.
Then, Vajrapāṇi, the great general of the yakṣas, with a smiling face and a countenance free from frowns, brandished his vajra.
He said this to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara:
“Blessed One, what is that true secret heart-mantra of Amoghapāśa, the lotus-uṣṇīṣa maṇḍala? Blessed One, please speak it.”
Then the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, perceiving the request of Vajrapāṇi, the great yakṣa general, touched his right hand to the lotus at his navel in the form of a mudrā.

As soon as he had touched it, a lotus appeared in his right hand, and upon that heart-mantra-lotus was seen the Lord himself, seated in his own form within a celestial palace, wearing the attire of Brahmā.
He possessed an unfailing form with three eyes and four arms, adorned with all ornaments, and [decked] with jewels and gold.
[He wears] a crown [with the syllable] ṆḌI; he is adorned with a crown [bearing the image of] Amitābha; his matted hair is adorned with a lotus-uṣṇīṣa crown;
and he is resplendent with a half-moon.
Holding a noose, wearing a lotus crown, holding a jewel-staff and a vajra-staff, seated in the full-lotus posture,
adorned with blazing garlands of light,
and clothed in various variegated garments whose eyes shine more intensely than the sun and moon.
Upon the two resplendent lotuses (12) 7,
it blazes intensely— delighting the hearts of all Tathāgatas,
worthy of veneration by all Bodhisattvas, worthy of worship by all deities, and worthy of being favored by all Nāgas.
It is to be gratified by all sense objects;
it is to be followed by all asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas;
it is to be delivered by all sentient beings.
Thus, in this vast expanse, the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara has revealed the heart that is the essence of reality.
Then, O Vajrapāṇi, as soon as the great yakṣa general Vajrapāṇi and that great assembly saw him, they all attained the secret heart-mantra of the Amoghapadma-vimaloṣṇīṣa-raśmijvāla-samādhi.
Having attained that samādhi, they all entered into the illusion-like samādhi; with their minds filled with joy, they prostrated at his feet and paid homage.
Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, the Noble Avalokiteśvara, spoke this mantra of the Heart of Amoghapāśa.
Oṃ! Padmoṣṇīṣa of the Amoghapāśa-hṛdaya, wearing the garb of a youth, Lord of the Lotus:
cause [the deity] to enter; O heart-mantra of the entire Amogha family and its samaya, grant all accomplishments infallibly!
Padma padma | Hūṃ hūṃ, homage to you, svāhā!
This is the Heart-Mantra of Amoghapāśa, the accomplishment through recitation for the attainment of siddhi.

Oṃ! Amoghapadmoṣṇīṣeśvara, Padmeśvara, summon all the Tathāgatas! Draw forth the pledge of Amoghapadmoṣṇīṣa, cause [them] to enter, and grant me the accomplishment of all activities! Śilākaragupta [says]: O Avalokiteśvara, hūṃ hūṃ! This is the mantra of the Family King Mahāpadmoṣṇīṣabhuja. || ||

Oṃ! O Mahācaṇḍapadmeśvara, you whose faces are terrifying with various forms, formidable lotus-fangs, and a fierce mien; devour all those with wicked hearts and obstacles, O Lotus-Bearer! Ciṭi dhṛṭi hūṃ svāhā!
This is the Wrathful King, the Heart-Essence of the Family.
The secret rites are in the inner circle.
Oṃ! Amoghapadmoṣṇīṣa, Great Lotus Noose Wrathful One, drive away [the obstacles]! Enter the ritual action! You who wear the garments of Mahāpaśupati, Yama, Varuṇa, Kubera, and Brahmā.
O Mahācaṇḍavega, in the lotus of the unerring family’s pledge, hūṃ hūṃ!
The heart-mantra of the Uṣṇīṣa of the Wrathful King Amoṣaghapāśapadma.
Now, the activities of the Amogha-hṛdaya come to pass merely by its being remembered; one will become equal and identical to all the Tathāgatas of the three times.
One’s physical form will be equal to that of Amitāyus. In all Buddha-fields throughout the ten directions, one proceeds as entirely equal and identical to all the Tathāgatas.
One is seen as equal to all Tathāgatas, indeed equal to the Peerless One.
Holding a lotus in the hand and placing the Padmoṣṇīṣa upon the hand, one becomes equal to Lokeśvara.
By truly binding the Padmoṣṇīṣa, one is consecrated on the head and body; indeed, one is consecrated by all the Tathāgatas of the three times.
He who, having recited the Heart of Padmoṣṇīṣa, obtains the unfailing consecration of the Padmoṣṇīṣas, attains hundreds of thousands of samādhis and unsurpassed glory.
Having honored the Kularāja mantra within the mandala, one should then worship Padmoṣṇīṣā.

There shall be the excellent accomplishment of the Kularāja for you, and in all matters concerning the excellent accomplishments of the Kularāja, the Kularājas, the Mantrarājas, and the supreme Vidyārājas will indeed appear;
they bestow all accomplishments and follow in accordance with Padmapāṇi, whereby the Amogha family is accomplished.
There is no doubt that [this] is accomplished through recitation alone.

In the Padmoṣṇīṣa family, within the sublime Padma maṇḍala, or in the Amoghapāśa maṇḍala, one becomes accomplished merely by reciting the mantra. By the mere recitation of the mantra, one becomes a Vidyādhara King of the Family-Kings, a Lord of Kings over all maṇḍalas, according to the ritual manual and mudrās of the Bodhisattvas.

The common lineage shall everywhere perform the affairs of kings; by means of this family lore (*kulavidyā*), one becomes a king in thousands and hundreds of Buddha-fields—fields as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā. One is eternally the lord of the gods among the gods, the lord of the hosts [of spirits], and likewise the master of the *yakṣas* and *rākṣasas*.
He will always be the sovereign king of the Gandharvas, Yakṣas, and likewise of the Rākṣasas everywhere; of this there is no doubt.
And he will be the family king of the Garuḍas, Kinnaras, and Mahoragas everywhere, until he abides in enlightenment.
Then, by the mere recollection of the King of Wrath, even Mount Sumeru would be instantly cast down by his fierce mind, and the Cakravāḍa mountains would be shattered;
from the agitation of the great ocean, a [new] ocean would arise.

All the abodes of the *nāgas* are set ablaze; all the *nāga* dwellings burn with everything. All the *vighnas*, *vināyakas*, *yakṣas*, *rākṣasas*, *bhūtas*, *grahas*, and terrible *apasmāras*—all of them go to destruction in a mere instant by the mere recollection of the King of Wrath (*krodharāja*).
Indeed, all the Kings of Wrath, together with the Guhyakas who abide by the family commitments (*kula-samaya*),
those established in the mudrās and positions within the maṇḍala, and whatever other mantra-deities there may be—
all of them go for refuge to the Vidyādharas merely by recollecting the King of Wrath.
All of them will follow,

whether they are standing, walking, or wherever they may stay: Śakra and the thirty-three gods, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Maheśvara, Yama, Varuṇa, Sāgara the king of the nāgas, Nanda and Upananda, and likewise Kumāra the commander of the army.
The four great kings always obey the vidyādhara; of this there is no doubt.
Whether it be all cruel deeds or even fierce deeds, success is seen therein by means of merely the syllable *hūṃ*.
Enemies, adversaries, wicked beings who are most terrible, hostile foreign armies, and those who hate people and commit sins—all these go to destruction and are reduced to ashes.

By the mere pressure of the syllable *hūṃ*, all wicked beings who are difficult to understand, ungrateful, and hostile toward those who have done them good, are all instantly consumed like moths by fire through the mere utterance of the fierce *hūṃ*.

Other thousands of rites, indeed hundreds of thousands of rites, are accomplished merely by recitation; indeed, they are accomplished instantly by mere remembrance. All rites are accomplished. || 5 ||
Then, by the mere recollection of Amoghapadmoṣṇīṣa, all undertakings will be accomplished twice over,
exactly as one directs the mind;
whatever action one may perform, it shall be so.
Whether it be a mandala or another location,
he performs his task everywhere in whatever manner accords with his intention.

Now, as the mantras are being set forth, all their respective activities are accomplished. Oṃ! All [mantras] of Amoghapāśa and Padmoṣṇīṣa in the maṇḍala—by the mere recollection of the single-syllable mantra of the Lord of the World, hundreds of thousands [of benefits are attained]. (15)
He will be established in the first stage.
Whatever dreadful hells have been accumulated through all manner of evil deeds,
they shall all perish, just as dust is scattered by the wind.
One attains all accomplishments;
one becomes a follower of all goals. The Tathāgatas and the other deities of the maṇḍala remain silent, while the noble Avalokiteśvara is eternally a granter of boons.
By the recollection of the mantra of the syllable Oṃ, one attains death and goes to the world-realm of Sukhāvatī; this is the single-syllable mantra.
Oṃ bhūḥ.
By reciting the two-syllable mantra one hundred thousand times, there will be the attainment of the second bhūmi;
one will stand in the presence of the Tathāgata Amitābha,
who will grant every boon.
It purifies all misdeeds,
one is liberated from previous illnesses,
and one attends upon Maṇibhadra, the lord of wealth, who has mastery over all.
Furthermore, no non-human being will ever again be able to create an obstacle for him;
having passed away, he is reborn on Mount Potalaka.
And one attains the accomplishment of the Amoghapāśa:
Oṃ Padme.
By reciting the three-syllable mantra one hundred thousand times, one enters the third stage (*bhūmi*),
and all the mudrās and mantras of the Lotus Array Mandala (*padmodāramaṇḍala*) are set in motion.
The noble Avalokiteśvara appears before him in the form of a youth and shall bestow all desired boons.
He reveals the Amoghapāśa-padmoṣṇīṣa maṇḍala;
he reveals all the secret maṇḍalas of the Tathāgatas; he shall bestow accomplishment everywhere.
Oṃ Padma Hrīḥ.
By reciting the four-syllable mantra one hundred thousand times, one ascends to the fourth bhūmi.
The noble Tathāgata Akṣobhya will stand before one with a body the color of gold;
extending his arm, he places his hand upon the crown of the head.
He will bestow a cry of "Well done! upon the Vidyādhara:
"Come, O Vidyādhara! All your obscurations of evil are purified;
your entire being is thoroughly cleansed and utterly pure."
From this human world, he will pass away and come to my buddha-field; he will be born with the recollection of his former births, and he shall never again be defiled by dwelling in a womb.
[He shall accomplish] all worldly tasks.
Success! || ||
Oṃ, to the one with the lotus hand!
By reciting the five-syllable mantra one hundred thousand times, you shall be established on the fifth stage.
The Tathāgata Padmottara, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, will grant you a vision;
[he will remove] all obscurations.
They go to complete exhaustion;
the Vidyādhara utters a sound of approval.
Excellent, excellent, Vidyādhara! A great mass of merit has been produced by you.
You, Vidyādhara, have planted great roots of virtue;
you, Vidyādhara, have transcended [the mundane].
Having planted roots of merit in the presence of ninety-two hundred thousand nayutas of kotis of Tathāgatas, you shall be born spontaneously in my buddha-fields.
You, Vidyādhara Nivāraṇa, have abandoned all evil.

You have accomplished the Amoghapāśa-padmoṣṇīṣa-hṛdaya-guhyamaṇḍala; perform all activities according to your desire within this chapter on the Great Mudrās. Whatever is in your mind, all that [shall be fulfilled].
"Thus, all means of accomplishment are well-accomplished."
Oṃ Padmāvalokite.
By reciting [the mantra] one hundred thousand times at the six forest retreats, one ascends to the state established upon the six stages (*ṣaḍbhūmi*).
It produces light for all the Tathāgatas;
as many Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas as there are atoms in a trichiliocosm mahāsāhasra world-system gaze upon him,
and he beholds them face-to-face.
And they will give [him] gifts and offer consolation.
Then the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Padmāvalokitadhvaja consoles that vidyādhara:
"Come, vidyādhara, to my buddha-field."
Until the end at the seat of enlightenment, you have brought your deeds to perfect completion. You have closed the gates of hell and opened for yourself the gates to all the Buddha-fields.

You have attained the commonality of the seed-family of all Tathāgatas; you have accomplished the secret maṇḍala of the heart-mantra of Amoghapāda and Padmoṣṇīṣa. The doors to all your abodes—both mundane and supramundane rites for the accomplishment of activities—have been opened for you.
As it abides in the mind: "Perform all activities!
Oṃ padmajvāla hūṃ dhṛk.
By reciting seven hundred thousand syllables immediately thereafter, one attains the samādhi named *Padmavimalavigatāvaraṇaśuddhi*.
By means of that attained samādhi,
the body will become brilliantly radiant, emitting rays of light of various colors.
He will become established on the seventh stage, and by the radiance of rays from his body, he will illuminate the entire great trichiliocosm, including all the abodes of the buddha-fields.
Wherever those rays fall, various rains of flowers, brilliant with diverse jewels and variegated precious gems,
shall appear, and offerings to all the Tathāgatas will proceed.
Then the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Vimalapadmājvalaraśmi, extending his golden-colored arms, places his right hand upon the head of the vidyādhara and grants him words of praise,
offering him consolation.
Excellent, excellent, Vidyādhara!
This is the supreme ritual for worship and recitation, the secret heart of the Blessed Buddhas;
this is the secret heart of the noble Avalokiteśvara, the essential mandala.
O Vidyādhara, you have accomplished the *Amoghapāda-padmoṣṇīṣa-hṛdaya*; the entire ritual manual (*kalpa*) of the *Padmoṣṇīṣa-hṛdaya* has been completed within this maṇḍala.
It was composed by Amoghapāśa.
"Go, Vidyādhara, and perform the work of a Buddha in my buddha-field."
Oṃ Amoghamaṇipadme.
By reciting the *Aṣṭamī-hṛdaya-dhāraṇī* one hundred thousand times, one becomes pure of body and stainless through mere recitation;
just as a great crystal jewel is perfectly pure both inside and out.
In this way, the body of the vidyādhara will become completely purified;
he will be established on the eighth stage (bhūmi).
The noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, with a perfectly pure physical form, will stand before the vidyādhara, manifesting his essential nature.
He consoles the vidyādhara,
places his right hand upon the crown of his head,
and gives him a word of praise.
"Excellent, excellent, O Vidyādhara who has entered into the supreme resolve! Come, O Vidyādhara, to the Buddha-field called *Samanubaddhalokavilokitā*.
There, you shall perform the work of a Buddha.
You have accomplished the secret heart-mantra and maṇḍala of the *Amoghapāśa-padmoṣṇīṣa*; now perform all activities, both mundane and supramundane, to the highest degree."
The means of accomplishment.
Oṃ padmalocane huru hūṃ.
By reciting the *Hṛdayadhāraṇī* of the ninth [chapter] one hundred thousand times, one will become established on the ninth stage (*bhūmi*).

One will become the eldest son of the noble Avalokiteśvara. One will have a direct vision of ninety-nine hundred thousand *koṭī-niyuta* of Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Perfectly Enlightened Ones, as well as of the Vidyādharas, and the various distinctions of the Buddhas.
He displays his miraculous power;
all the Vidyādharas place their hands upon his head.
And they will give their approval, saying:

"Excellent, excellent, O Great Vidyādhara! You have accomplished all these things that were taught by the Leader of the World for the attainment of Buddhahood—both mundane and supramundane—through this ritual procedure for the Maṇḍala of Amoghapāśa, according to the rules and instructions of the Sūtra. (7)
Oṃ padmoṣṇīṣavimale hūṃ phaṭ.
For one who performs one hundred thousand recitations of the ten-syllable heart mantra,
having become irreversible, they shall abide established upon the ten stages (bhūmis).
He is to be called a Tathāgata by the beings among gods and humans;
he is irreversible.
"In this regard, there will be the turning of the wheel of the Unfailing Lotus Uṣṇīṣa toward unexcelled, perfect enlightenment; of this there is no doubt."

This is indeed the practice of the ten mantras; it is the unsurpassed accomplishment of reality (*tattvasiddhi*). Merely by recitation, they are accomplished. I have previously explained all these transformations of the *Amoghapāśahṛdaya* for one who is pure, whose conduct is clean, and who wears clean garments;
who generates a mind of loving-kindness and compassion, speaks the truth, is affectionate toward his guru, is devoted to faith in the Three Jewels, and constantly worships his guru and teacher.
This is declared to be the procedure for recitation, which is the unsurpassed awakening of the Buddha.
Then indeed, Vajrapāṇi, the great yakṣa general, and the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, with a smiling face and brandishing his vajra, spoke thus to those with bowed heads:
"O Mahāsattva, these ten mantra-words of the dhāraṇīs—the Amoghapāśa, Padmoṣṇīṣa, Maṇḍala, and Hṛdaya—are exceedingly difficult to obtain; they are the vast and profound secret."

By merely reciting this *dhāraṇī-hṛdaya* from their hearts even once, they will perform the Buddha’s work; how much more so, O Avalokiteśvara, for those who accomplish the extensive procedures for the practice of recitation with great effort and fatigue?
Having observed the fast day and night, and having consumed alms-food, fruits, tubers, and roots, one shall accomplish this *vidyā*.
"O Lord of the World, tell me, what accomplishment arises for him?
Avalokiteśvara said:
Listen, Vajrapāṇi! Merely by means of fasting and recitation for a day and night—that is, in just a single day—the accomplishment of the fruit arises.

Vajrapāṇi, whichever son of good family or daughter of good family, monk or nun, layman or laywoman, or anyone else—whether a shaven-headed ascetic, one living off a family, a Brahmin, a Kṣatriya, a woman, a man, a boy, a girl, a Vaiśya, or a Śūdra—who [practices] for even a single moment or instant...
Whether for a moment, or for one session, or for the full three sessions without speaking;

whether one will remember this chapter on the heart-mantra and wrathful-family mantra of the Amoghapāśa Padmoṣṇīṣa even once, or recite it, or even merely recall its name— [The Blessed One said: "O son of good family, if there is anyone who, having heard this Dharma-discourse, shall write it down, cause it to be written, read it, or cause it to be read; or if, having heard it, they shall uphold it, retain it in memory, recite it, teach it extensively to others, and practice it according to the instructions, then, O son of good family, that person shall be protected by me with my own body, and by all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas. Furthermore, O son of good family, that person shall be freed from all diseases, and shall not be afflicted by any calamities, such as kings, thieves, fire, water, poison, weapons, or enemies. They shall be liberated from all evil rebirths and shall attain birth in the realm of Sukhāvatī."

Vajrapāṇi, by merely remembering him even for a single session, even one who has committed the five deeds of immediate retribution and is destined for the Avīci hell and will remain there for an eon— his everything shall be purified.
He will exhaust all accumulated obscurations and the veils of evil,
and he will come to possess a completely pure and stainless body.
They will be free from the evil of obscurations;
upon the transition of death and rebirth, they will be born spontaneously within lotuses in the world-realm of Sukhāvatī,
and they will possess the recollection of their past lives.
Furthermore, there shall never again be any going to an evil rebirth.
For eighty hundred thousand eons, he shall be a supreme universal monarch (cakravartin),
and there shall never again be any going to an evil rebirth.
For eighty hundred thousand kalpas, he experiences happiness in the world-system Sukhāvatī; for sixty-two hundred thousand kalpas, he experiences happiness in the world-system Abhirati;
and for seventy-two hundred thousand kalpas, he is reborn in the world-system Lokavilokitā.
He will be one who remembers his births (jātismara).
For twelve hundred thousand kalpas he will be a universal monarch (cakravartin) named Maṇidhara.
For eighteen thousand kalpas he will experience happiness in the abode of the noble Avalokiteśvara on Mount Potalaka.
(20) For nine hundred and ninety thousand kalpas, he will be reborn among the Akaniṣṭha devas;
for eighty hundred thousand kalpas, he will experience happiness among the Tuṣita devas;
and for a hundred thousand kalpas, he will exercise the sovereignty of Śakra among the Trāyastriṃśa devas.
For fifty-two hundred thousand kalpas, he traverses all the Buddha-fields in the ten directions. For twenty thousand kalpas, he enjoys the sovereignty of a universal monarch (*cakravartin*).
Furthermore, he never again takes birth within a mother’s womb; wherever he is born, he is always born spontaneously (*upapāduka*).

In all [lives], O Vajrapāṇi, he will be one who remembers his births and former existences. Thus, by the mere recollection of this single vidyā, he will become endowed with a great mass of merit consisting of roots of virtue.
If anyone, O Vajrapāṇi, should dwell for a single night...
Or if one shall perform a single fast and recitation,
O Vajrapāṇi, in this very life,
within this human existence, he shall attain the samādhi called "The Great Unfailing Pure One" (Mahāmogha-vimala), which has not been previously attained.
He attains the Amoghavyūha-samādhi; he attains the Padmojjvalavikurvaṇa-samādhi;
he attains the samādhi named Amoghavimalanirbhāsa.
He attains the samādhi named Amoghavilokitadhvaja; he attains the samādhi named Padmoṣṇīṣaviratadhvaja;
and he attains the accomplishment of the secret heart-mantra of the Amoghajvalanoṣṇīṣa.
Furthermore, he will have planted roots of merit in the presence of ninety-two hundred thousand nayutas of kotis of Tathāgatas, equal in number to the sands of the river Ganges.
He will be endowed with a great mass of merit; in his next birth, he will be born spontaneously from lotuses in the world-system Sukhāvatī.
And this is the ritual manual for the Heart-mantra of Amoghapāśa.
The Amoghapadmoṣṇīṣa Maṇḍala, the ritual manual for the Vimokṣa Maṇḍala, and the entire ritual manual for the Mudrās shall remain present before one’s eyes in their entirety.
One will become an Amogha Vidyādhara Cakravartin. || ||
The procedure for the practice of the heart-mantra in the Padmoṣṇīṣa-maṇḍala of Amoghapāśahṛdaya;
the second procedure for the practice. (21)
